title: The Frohmanian Tether on SDiff(T^3): A Metriplectic Correction, Its Canonicity, and an Obstruction to Damping
notes: Copyright (c) 2026 Benjamin Stanley Frohman. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. This record is NOT a proof of global regularity of the 3D Navier-Stokes equations and makes no claim toward the Clay Millennium Problem.
description: PREPRINT (work in progress). Version 0.1.4 (new version of 10.5281/zenodo.24102715) adds the Lean module ExplicitFlows; no existing Lean statement was changed. ALL MAIN RESULTS ARE CONDITIONAL. Lean 4 (v4.30.0-rc1) / Mathlib (v4.30.0-rc1, rev 0c154d67103f74be3a0f2c509f72ccbf5be9f2a7) formalization of conditional statements about the Frohmanian tether T(F,G) = -kappa ||omega||^2 int <Pi_u dF, Pi_u dG>, a symmetric quadratic correction to the Arnold Lie-Poisson bracket. The functional derivative is the unique divergence-free L2 gradient along smooth compactly supported test fields (0 where none exists). Proved: symmetry and negative feedback (C3) unconditionally; nondegeneracy of T, polarization of T on functionals with gradients, saturation, projection-dependence and the canonical density of T; a family of smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free test fields curl(chi e_2) concentrated at any point with any radius, and with it the corrected weight condition AEEnstrophyWeight TetherKernel (every locally integrable density of T equals -kappa ||omega||^2 almost everywhere); the transported (equivariant) form of (C1), T(g.omega; F o g^-1, G o g^-1) = T(omega; F, G), for all translations (via translation equivariance of the functional gradient and of Biot-Savart); canonicity only inside a restricted kernel class (from diagonal saturation and polarization); and an obstruction to damping: every symmetric kernel satisfying (C2) has B(H,M) = 0 for every functional M. Refuted in Lean: (C1) with the functionals held fixed (for T, under translations), dH/dw = u, transitivity on Casimir levels, the pointwise strain bound |Du(x)| <= C ||omega||_inf, unrestricted polarization of T, the pointwise weight hypothesis, the a.e. weight hypothesis over all (possibly non-measurable) densities (Vitali-set density), and Step1Hyp; also removed: TetherIntegralPreserved, a circular Jacobi lemma, an antisymmetric uniqueness clause and a uniform lower bound on local existence times. New in 0.1.4, proved: the decaying shear flow e^{-nu k^2 t}(a sin(k x_2), 0, 0) with constant pressure and the decaying ABC (Beltrami) flow e^{-nu k^2 t}(A sin k x_2 + C cos k x_1, B sin k x_0 + A cos k x_2, C sin k x_1 + B cos k x_0) with pressure -|u|^2/2 solve the library's Navier-Stokes equations for all t >= 0 (shearFlow_navier_stokes, abcFlow_navier_stokes; hence NS_PDE_On for every T), are nonzero (shearFlow_ne_zero, abcFlow_ne_zero), the ABC profile satisfies curl u = k u (curl_abcProfile), and for k = 2 pi m both are global smooth Z^3-periodic solutions in the class of Clay_B_exact for these particular data (shearFlow_isPeriodicSmoothSolution, abcFlow_isPeriodicSmoothSolution, clay_B_instance_shear, clay_B_instance_abc). Also proved: no continuous nonzero Z^3-periodic field has finite energy on R^3 (not_integrable_sq_of_periodic), so KatoLocalWitness u0 nu is empty for every nonzero periodic u0 (isEmpty_katoLocalWitness_of_periodic): the shear and ABC flows are NOT Kato witnesses, and at such data LocalTetherBound, SmoothPhysicalUniqueness and BKMGlobalContinuation hold only vacuously (recorded as an audit, not as discharges). PeriodicTetherClosingBound is not discharged even at these data (uniqueness of smooth periodic solutions is not formalized). Open hypotheses, by Lean name: (b) classical results not in Mathlib: KatoLocalWitness (hKato), BKMGlobalContinuation, SmoothPhysicalUniqueness, PeriodicBKMContinuation, KatoUniquenessOnExistenceTimes, IsCoadjointMotion; (d) as strong as the open problem: LocalTetherRate, LocalTetherBound, LocalTetherClosingBound, PeriodicTetherClosingBound, PeriodicDirectionDepletionBound, and the global-path forms FrohmanianTetherRate, FrohmanianTetherBound, FrohmanianTetherClosingBound, RiccatiMajorantExists; (c) kernel-class conditions on a competitor B in the canonicity theorems (PolarizesOnDifferentiable, SaturatesTetherQuadratic, h_proj, h_density, AEEnstrophyWeight B); open for T itself: DegenerateWRTKineticEnergy TetherKernel (C2) at regular vorticities, and transport-invariance under rotations and general volume-preserving diffeomorphisms (not formalized). Auxiliary lemmas not stated in the paper additionally take named, unproved Props as explicit hypotheses (BKMContinuationCriterion, LocalExistenceTime, SmoothBelowTstar, PathBKMIntegrable, TstarIsTop, KatoUniformRestart, UniformVorticityCeiling, FiniteTimeVorticityBound and their Physical/Local forms, ClassicalStretchingSource, CorrectedMaxRate, SymplecticQuarticStretchingSinkAtMax, Clay_B_exact_with_energy, ZeroDerivAlongEnergy, and regularity side conditions); see the paper, Section 11.1. No Jacobi identity is claimed.
